$comment: The runtimeVersions of binaries that are actually OUT THERE — in the store, or on a
tester's phone. This file is the only thing CI can consult to answer 'would anyone
receive this update?', and getting that wrong is invisible: a publish aimed at a
runtimeVersion nobody has succeeds, reports success, and reaches no one.
It exists because the honest source — asking EAS which builds exist — needs an
EXPO_TOKEN that has to be minted by hand in a browser, and a check nobody can run
without a secret is a check that will be skipped. A committed list is auditable, moves
in the same PR as the release it describes, and is wrong only in the safe direction:
a forgotten entry stops a publish, it does not push a bad one.
ADD AN ENTRY when you upload a build to the store or hand an APK to testers. REMOVE
one when no device can still be running it — an entry left behind only means CI is
willing to publish for a runtimeVersion nobody has, which is harmless but pointless.
